As for His saying: ﴿وَالسَّارِقُ وَالسَّارِقَةُ فَاقْطَعُوا أَيْدِيَهما﴾, the proper way in it is the nominative, because it is not specific (muwaqqat), so it is put in the nominative as the conditional is, as when you say: من سرق فاقطعوا يده ("whoever steals, cut off his hand"). Likewise His saying ﴿والشعراءُ يَتَّبِعُهُم الغاوون﴾, whose meaning — and Allah knows best — is: whoever (composes poetry), the erring follow him.
Had you put His saying (والسارقَ والسارقَة) in the accusative by the verb, it would be correct.
And His saying ﴿وكلَّ إنسانٍ ألزمناه طائِرَهُ فى عُنُقه﴾: with (كل) the Arabs prefer the nominative, whether or not the verb has fallen on a returning pronoun. I heard the Arabs say (وكُلُّ شَىْءٍ أحْصَيْنَاهُ فى إمَامٍ مُبِينٍ) in the nominative, though a pronoun returns to it. And they recited to me, concerning a case where the verb did not fall on a returning pronoun:
فقالوا تَعَرّفْها المنازِلَ مِن مِنىً * وما كلُّ من يَغْشَى مِنىً أنا عارِفُ
ألِفْنا دِيارا لم تكن مِن ديارِنا * ومن يُتَأَلّفْ بالكرامَةِ يَأْلَفُ
(They said: "Seek her out among the lodgings of Minā" — but I do not know everyone who comes to Minā. We have grown fond of abodes that were not our abodes; and whoever is won over with generosity grows fond.)
So (عارف) did not fall on كلّ; that is because in (كل) there is the sense: "and there is no one coming to Minā whom I know". Had it been accusative, it would be correct, but I have heard it only in the nominative. And another said:
قد عَلِقَت أمُّ الخِيارِ تدّعِى * علىّ ذنبا كلُّه لم أَصنعِ
(Umm al-Khiyār has taken to claiming against me a sin, none of which I did.)
in the nominative; and one of Banū Asad recited it to me in the accusative.
And His saying: ﴿قُلْ إِنَّ ٱلأَمْرَ كُلَّهُ للَّهِ﴾: whoever puts it in the nominative makes (كل) a noun and puts it in the nominative by the lām in لِلّه, like His saying ﴿ويومَ القيامة تَرَى الذِين كَذَبُوا على اللهِ وجوههم مسودّة﴾; and whoever puts (كله) in the accusative makes it a qualifier [tawkīd (emphasis)] of الأمر.

farraa:156-156.t:
His saying: ﴿يٰأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ آمَنُواْ لاَ تَكُونُواْ كَٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ وَقَالُواْ لإِخْوَانِهِمْ إِذَا ضَرَبُواْ فِي ٱلأَرْضِ﴾: by the [normal] standard of Arabic it should have been said: وقالوا لإخوانهم إذ ضربوا فى الأرض, because it is past, as you say: ضربتك إذ قمت ("I struck you when you stood up"), and you do not say ضربتك إذا قمت. Yet that is permissible, and what is in the Book of Allah is good Arabic, because "saying", though past in form, is future in meaning, since (الذين) is taken in the sense of the conditional, like مَنْ and ما. You say to a man: أحبِب من أحبَّك ("love whoever loves you") and أحبب كلّ رجل أحبَّك ("love every man who loves you"); the verb is past and is suitable for the future, since the persons concerned are not specific. Were you to make it specific, it would not be permissible. Of that is your saying: لأضربن هذا الذى ضربك إذ سلَّمت عليك ("I will surely strike this one who struck you when you greeted him"), because you have made it specific, so the conditional sense has fallen away from it. And you say: لا تضرب إلا الذى ضربك إذا سلمت عليه ("strike only the one who strikes you when you greet him"), saying (إذا) because you have not made it specific. Likewise His saying: ﴿إِنّ الذِين كَفَرُوا ويَصُدُّون عَنْ سَبيل الله﴾: He said ﴿ويَصُدُّون﴾ and referred it back to (كفروا) because it is not specific. Likewise His saying ﴿إِلاَّ الذِين تابوا من قَبلِ أن تَقْدِروا عليهِم﴾, the meaning being: except those who repent before you have power over them.
And Allah knows best. Likewise His saying ﴿إِلاَّ مَنْ تَابَ وَآمَنَ وعَمِلَ صَالِحا﴾, meaning: except whoever repents and does righteous deeds. And the poet said:
فإنى لآتيكم تشَكُّرَ ما مضى * مِن الأَمرِ واستِيجابَ ما كان فى غدِ
(I come to you in gratitude for what has passed of the matter, and to earn what will be tomorrow.)
He means the future by it; therefore he said (كان فى غد). Had it been past, he would have said: ما كان فى أمس ("what was yesterday"), and ما كان فى غد would not be permissible. As for the saying of al-Kumayt:
ماذاقَ بُؤسَ معِيشةٍ ونعيمها * فيما مَضَى أَحدٌ إذا لم يَعْشقِ
(No one has tasted the misery and bliss of life in the past if he has not loved.)
it is of that kind; he only meant: he has not tasted it in the past and will not taste it in the future if he has not loved.
And you say: ما هلك امرؤ عرف قدره ("no man perishes who knows his worth"); if you introduced (إذا) into this, it would be better than (إذ), because you are not reporting that about one person — [which would call for إذ] — but have made it like a habitual practice, so past and future both apply. «[Translator's note: the source reads فيكونَ بإذا "so that it would be with إذا"; the sense requires إذ here, and it is translated accordingly.]» Of that is a man's saying to another: كنتَ صابرا إذا ضربتك ("you used to be patient when I struck you"), because the meaning is: whenever you were struck, you were patient. But when you say: كنت صابرا إذ ضُرِبت ("you were patient when you were struck"), you are only reporting his patience in a single beating.

farraa:159-159.t:
His saying: ﴿فَبِمَا رَحْمَةٍ مِّنَ ٱللَّهِ لِنتَ لَهُمْ﴾: the Arabs make (ما) a ṣila (redundant connective) with the definite and the indefinite alike.
Allah said ﴿فبِما نَقْضِهِمْ ميثاقَهُمْ﴾, the meaning being فبنقضِهِم ("for their breaking"), and ﴿عَمَّا قَليلٍ لَيُصْبِحُنّ نادِمِينَ﴾, the meaning being: عن قليل ("after a little"). And Allah knows best. Sometimes they treat it as a noun while it is in the manner of a ṣila; so what follows it may be nominative as its ṣila (relative clause), or genitive, by making the ṣila follow what precedes it; as the poet said:
فكفى بنا فضلا على من غيرِنا * حبُّ النبِىّ محمدٍ إيانا
(It suffices us as a distinction over others than us that the Prophet Muḥammad loves us.)
You put (غير) in the nominative if you make it a ṣila by implying (هو), and in the genitive by following مَنْ. And al-Farazdaq said:
إنى وإياك إن بلَّغن أرحُلَنا * كمن بِواديه بعد المَحْل ممطورِ
(I and you, if they [the camels] bring our saddles [to you], are like one whose valley has been rained on after drought.)
This is with indefinites. When the ṣila is definite, they prefer the nominative. Of that is (فَبِما نَقْضِهِمْ): no one read it in the nominative and we have not heard it; but had it been said, it would be permissible. They recited to us the verse of ʿAdī:
لم أَرَ مثل الفتيان فى غِيَرِ الـ * أيامِ يَنْسَوْنَ ما عواقبُها
(I have not seen the like of young men amid the vicissitudes of days: they forget what their outcomes are.)
The meaning is: they forget their outcomes, [عواقبها] being the ṣila of ما. This is something I dislike, because whoever says it would be obliged to say: ﴿أيّما الأجلان قضيت﴾ [with the nominative]; so I dislike it for that reason, but I do not reject it, for it has occurred. Some of the grammarians have explained it as: they forget what thing their outcomes are; and that is permissible, but the first interpretation is dearer to me.
The readers do not read with everything that is permissible in Arabic; so do not let the denunciation of a denouncer make ugly in your eyes what is permissible but has not been read by the readers.

farraa:161-161.t: His saying: ﴿وَمَا كَانَ لِنَبِيٍّ أَنْ يَغُلَّ﴾: some of the people of Medina read أن يُغَلَّ, meaning: that he be betrayed. The companions of ʿAbd Allāh also read it so: أن يُغَلَّ, meaning: that he be stolen from or charged with betrayal. That is permissible even though it is not said يُغَلَّل [in the intensive form], so it is like His saying: ﴿فإنهم لا يكذِّبونك - ويُكْذِبونك﴾. Ibn ʿAbbās and Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Sulamī read "أن يَغُلَّ"; that is because on the day of Uḥud they supposed that the spoils would not be divided among them as had been done on the day of Badr. Its meaning is: that he be accused and it be said, "He has misappropriated."

farraa:163-163.t: His saying: ﴿هُمْ دَرَجَاتٌ عِندَ ٱللَّهِ﴾: He is saying: they differ in merit; some of them are higher than others.

farraa:164-164.t: His saying: ﴿وَيُزَكِّيهِمْ﴾: He takes zakāt from them; as the Blessed and Exalted said: ﴿خُذْ مِنْ أموالِهِم صَدَقَةً تُطَهِّرُهُمْ وتُزَكّيهِم بها﴾.

farraa:165-165.t: His saying: ﴿قُلْ هُوَ مِنْ عِندِ أَنْفُسِكُمْ﴾: He is saying: you abandoned what you were commanded, sought the spoils and left your posts; so the harm came to you from your own side.

farraa:167-167.t: His saying: ﴿قَاتِلُواْ فِي سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِ أَوِ ٱدْفَعُواْ﴾: He is saying: increase your numbers, for if you increase your numbers you will repel the enemy by your great number.

farraa:169-170.t:
His saying: ﴿بَلْ أَحْيَاءٌ عِندَ رَبِّهِمْ يُرْزَقُونَ﴾ and His saying: ﴿فَرِحِينَ﴾: [had it been nominative, as "بل أحياء فرحون", it would be permissible. Its accusative is by detachment (inqiṭāʿ) from the hāʾ in "ربهم"; or, if you wish, [it is a ḥāl of] يرزقون: يرزقون فرحين ("they are provided for, rejoicing")] ﴿وَيَسْتَبْشِرُونَ بِٱلَّذِينَ لَمْ يَلْحَقُواْ بِهِم مِّنْ خَلْفِهِمْ﴾: of their brethren, for whom they hope for martyrdom because of what they have seen of Allah's reward; so they rejoice over them.
And His saying: ﴿أَلاَّ خَوْفٌ عَلَيْهِمْ﴾: they rejoice for them that there is no fear upon them "nor grief".

farraa:171-171.t: His saying: ﴿وَفَضْلٍ وَأَنَّ ٱللَّهَ لاَ يُضِيعُ أَجْرَ ٱلْمُؤْمِنِينَ﴾ is read with fatḥa and with kasra. Whoever gives it fatḥa makes it genitive, following النعمة; whoever gives it kasra begins afresh. It is the reading of ʿAbd Allāh: "والله لا يضيع", and this is an argument for whoever reads with kasra.

farraa:173-173.t: His saying: ﴿ٱلَّذِينَ قَالَ لَهُمُ ٱلنَّاسُ﴾: (الناس) in this place is one person, namely Nuʿaym ibn Masʿūd al-Ashjaʿī. Abū Sufyān and his companions sent him and said: "Discourage Muḥammad ﷺ, or frighten him, so that he does not meet us at the Lesser Badr" — which had been an appointment between them [made] on the day of Uḥud. Nuʿaym came to them and said: "They came to you in your own town and did to you what they did; so how will it be with you when you come upon them in their town, while they are more and you are fewer?" So Allah, Blessed and Exalted, revealed: ﴿إِنَّمَا ذٰلِكُمُ ٱلشَّيْطَانُ يُخَوِّفُ أَوْلِيَاءَهُ﴾.

farraa:175-175.t: As for His saying: ﴿إِنَّمَا ذٰلِكُمُ ٱلشَّيْطَانُ يُخَوِّفُ أَوْلِيَاءَهُ﴾: He is saying: he frightens you with his allies, "so do not fear them". Similar to that is His saying: ﴿لِينذِر يوم التلاقِ﴾, meaning: to warn you of the Day of Meeting; and His saying: ﴿لِينذِر بأسا شدِيدا﴾, the meaning being: to warn you of severe might; the might is not warned, rather one is warned with it.

farraa:178-178.t: His saying: ﴿وَلاَ يَحْسَبَنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ أَنَّمَا نُمْلِي لَهُمْ خَيْرٌ لأَنْفُسِهِمْ﴾: whoever reads "ولا تحسبن" says "إنما" [with kasra]. Some have read it "ولا تحسبن الذِين كفرا أنما" with tāʾ and with fatḥa, by way of repetition: do not suppose them — do not suppose that what We grant them in respite...; and it is like His saying: ﴿هَلْ يَنْظُرُونَ إِلاَّ السَّاعَةَ أَنْ تَأْتِيَهُم﴾, by repetition: are they waiting for anything but that it come upon them? «[Translator's note: the source has كفرا, evidently a misprint for كفروا.]»

farraa:179-179.t: His saying: ﴿مَّا كَانَ ٱللَّهُ لِيَذَرَ ٱلْمُؤْمِنِينَ عَلَىٰ مَآ أَنْتُمْ عَلَيْهِ﴾: the polytheists said to the Prophet ﷺ: "Why is it that you claim that a man among us is in the Fire, and when he goes over to you and becomes Muslim you say: 'He is in Paradise'? So tell us who among us will come to you before he comes to you, so that we may know them." So Allah, Blessed and Exalted, revealed: ﴿مَّا كَانَ ٱللَّهُ لِيَذَرَ ٱلْمُؤْمِنِينَ﴾ in the state you speak of, O polytheists, "حتّى يَميزَ الْخَبِيثَ مِنَ الطّيِّبِ"; then He said: Allah was not going to inform you of that and acquaint you with His unseen.

farraa:180-180.t:
His saying: ﴿وَلاَ يَحْسَبَنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ يَبْخَلُونَ بِمَآ آتَاهُمُ ٱللَّهُ مِن فَضْلِهِ هُوَ خَيْراً لَّهُمْ﴾: [it may be said: "هو" here is only a ʿimād (support pronoun), so where is the noun of this ʿimād? It is answered: it is implied; its meaning is: let the misers not suppose that miserliness is better for them]. So the mention of يبخلون sufficed in place of البخل; as you say in ordinary speech: قدم فلان فسُرِرت به ("so-and-so arrived and I was pleased by it") while you mean: I was pleased by his arrival. And the poet said:
إِذا نُهى السفِيهُ جَرَى إليه * وخالف، والسفِيهُ إلى خِلافِ
(When the fool is forbidden, he runs toward it [folly] and disobeys; and the fool tends to disobedience.)
He means: toward folly. This is frequent in speech.
And His saying: ﴿سَيُطَوَّقُونَ مَا بَخِلُواْ بِهِ﴾: it is said that it is the zakāt: the one who withheld it will come on the Day of Resurrection with a bald serpent wound around his neck, with two black spots over its eyes, biting his cheeks and saying: "I am the zakāt that you withheld from me." «[Translator's note: بفيه زبيبتان literally "in its mouth two zabības"; the hadith wording describes the two spots or venom-swellings of the serpent.]»
And His saying: ﴿وَللَّهِ مِيرَاثُ ٱلسَّمَاوَاتِ وَٱلأَرْضِ﴾: the meaning is: Allah causes the people of the heavens and the people of the earth to die, and He alone remains. That is His inheritance, Blessed and Exalted: that He remains and everything perishes.

farraa:181-181.t: His saying: ﴿سَنَكْتُبُ مَا قَالُواْ﴾: it has also been read "سيُكتب ما قالوا"; Ḥamza read it so, taking it into account because it is [so] in the Copy of ʿAbd Allāh.

farraa:183-183.t:
His saying: ﴿حَتَّىٰ يَأْتِيَنَا بِقُرْبَانٍ تَأْكُلُهُ ٱلنَّارُ﴾: this used to be. The offering (القربان) [was consumed by] a fire with a rustling and a loud sound which used to descend upon some of the prophets. «[Translator's note: the source literally says "the offering is a fire…"; the bracketed words follow the evident sense.]»
When they said that to the Prophet ﷺ, Allah, Blessed and Exalted, said: "Say", O Muḥammad: ﴿قَدْ جَآءَكُمْ رُسُلٌ مِّن قَبْلِي بِٱلْبَيِّنَاتِ﴾ and with the offering you spoke of; ﴿فَلِمَ قَتَلْتُمُوهُمْ إِن كُنتُمْ صَادِقِينَ﴾.

farraa:188-188.t:
His saying: ﴿لاَ تَحْسَبَنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ يَفْرَحُونَ بِمَآ أَتَوْاْ وَّيُحِبُّونَ أَن يُحْمَدُواْ بِمَا لَمْ يَفْعَلُواْ﴾: He is saying: in what they did [أتوا meaning "did"]; as He said: ﴿لقد جئتِ شيئا فرِيا﴾, and like His saying: ﴿واللذان يَأْتِيانِها مِنكم﴾; and in the reading of ʿAbd Allāh: "فمن أتى فاحشة فعله". And His saying: ﴿ويُحِبُّون أَن يُحْمَدُوا بِما لم يفعلوا﴾: they said, "We are the people of the first knowledge and the first prayer"; they say that and do not acknowledge Muḥammad ﷺ. That is His saying: ﴿ويُحِبُّون أن يُحْمدوا بِما لم يَفْعَلُوا﴾.
And His saying: ﴿فَلاَ تَحْسَبَنَّهُمْ بِمَفَازَةٍ مِّنَ ٱلْعَذَابِ﴾: He is saying: far from the punishment.
(He said: al-Farrāʾ said: Whoever claims that أو in this verse is in other than the sense of بل has fabricated a lie against Allah, because Allah, Blessed and Exalted, does not doubt; and from it is the saying of Allah, Blessed and Exalted: ﴿وأرسلناه إلى مِائةِ ألفٍ أَو يزِيدون﴾.) «[Translator's note: the verse under discussion contains no أو; this parenthetical note evidently belongs to the comment on al-Ṣāffāt 37:147, which it quotes.]»

farraa:191-191.t: His saying: ﴿ٱلَّذِينَ يَذْكُرُونَ ٱللَّهَ قِيَاماً وَقُعُوداً وَعَلَىٰ جُنُوبِهِمْ﴾: someone may ask: how did He coordinate [a phrase] with على onto nouns? It is said: it is in the sense of nouns; do you not see that His saying ﴿وَعَلَىٰ جُنُوبِهِمْ﴾ means: "and lying down"? Likewise He coordinated nouns with their like in another place, saying: "دعانا لِجنْبِه", meaning: lying on his side, "أو قاعدا أو قائما". So لجنبه and على جنبه are the same.

farraa:193-193.t: His saying: ﴿يُنَادِي لِلإِيمَانِ﴾ is as He said: "الذى هدانا لهذا" and "أوْحَى لهَا", meaning إليها ("to it"), and هدانا إلى هذا ("guided us to this").

farraa:196-196.t: His saying: ﴿لاَ يَغُرَّنَّكَ تَقَلُّبُ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ فِي ٱلْبِلاَدِ﴾: the Jews used to travel through the land and acquire wealth, so Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: let that not deceive you.

farraa:197-197.t: His saying: ﴿مَتَاعٌ قَلِيلٌ﴾: in this world.

farraa:198-198.t: His saying: ﴿نُزُلاً مِّنْ عِندِ ٱللَّهِ﴾ and (ثوابا) issue from the meaning: "they have that as a hospitable gift and as a reward", as an explicative; as you say: هو لك هبةً وبيعا وصدقة ("it is yours as a gift, a sale and alms").

farraa:199-199.t: His saying: ﴿خَاشِعِينَ للَّهِ﴾ means: they believe in Him, humbly submissive.

farraa:200-200.t: His saying: ﴿يَا أَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ آمَنُواْ ٱصْبِرُواْ﴾: with your Prophet, in jihad; (وصابِروا): [outlast] your enemy, so that he is not more steadfast than you.

farraa:2-2.t: His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿ٱللَّهُ لاۤ إِلَـٰهَ إِلاَّ هُوَ ٱلْحَيُّ ٱلْقَيُّومُ﴾ — Muḥammad ibn al-Jahm narrated to us from al-Farrāʾ: (al-ḥayyu al-qayyūmu) is the reading of the generality; ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb and Ibn Masʿūd read it "al-qayyām." The pattern of al-qayyūm is fayʿūl, and al-qayyām is fayʿāl, and both are praise. The people of the Hijaz most often say fayʿāl from three-radical words; so they say for al-ṣawwāgh (the goldsmith): al-ṣayyāgh.

farraa:7-7.t:
His saying: ﴿هُوَ ٱلَّذِيۤ أَنزَلَ عَلَيْكَ ٱلْكِتَابَ مِنْهُ آيَاتٌ مُّحْكَمَاتٌ﴾ — ﴿مِنْهُ آيَاتٌ مُّحْكَمَاتٌ﴾ means: making clear the lawful and the unlawful, and they have not been abrogated. They are the three verses in al-Anʿām, the first of which is: ﴿قل تعالَوا أَتل ما حرّم ربّكم عليكم﴾, and the two verses after it.
His saying: ﴿هُنَّ أُمُّ ٱلْكِتَابِ﴾ — He says: they are the foundation.
﴿وَأُخَرُ مُتَشَابِهَاتٌ﴾ — and they are: Alif-Lām-Mīm-Ṣād, Alif-Lām-Rā, and Alif-Lām-Mīm-Rā. They were ambiguous to the Jews because they sought the duration of this community's sustenance [Translator's note: i.e. its lifespan] from the abjad reckoning (ḥisāb al-jummal); when it did not come out for them as they wished, they said: Muḥammad ﷺ has confused things, and they disbelieved in Muḥammad ﷺ.
So Allah said: ﴿فَيَتَّبِعُونَ مَا تَشَابَهَ مِنْهُ ٱبْتِغَاءَ ٱلْفِتْنَةِ وَٱبْتِغَاءَ تَأْوِيلِهِ﴾, meaning the explanation of the duration.
Then He said: ﴿وَمَا يَعْلَمُ تَأْوِيلَهُ إِلاَّ ٱللَّهُ﴾, then began afresh with "wa-l-rāsikhūna," putting them in the nominative by "yaqūlūna," not by making them follow the case of "Allah." In the reading of Ubayy: "ويقول الراسخون" ("and the firmly grounded say"), and in the reading of ʿAbdullāh: "إنْ تأويله إلا عند الله، والراسخون فى العلم يقولون" ("its interpretation is only with Allah, and those firmly grounded in knowledge say").

farraa:11-11.t: His saying: ﴿كَدَأْبِ آلِ فِرْعَوْنَ﴾ — He says: the Jews disbelieved like the disbelief of Pharaoh's people and their way.

farraa:12-12.t:
His saying: ﴿قُلْ لِّلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ سَتُغْلَبُونَ﴾ — it is read with the tāʾ and the yāʾ. Whoever reads it with the yāʾ takes it as addressed to the Jews, and as meaning that the defeat is of the idolaters [after] the day of Uḥud. That is because when the Prophet ﷺ routed the idolaters on the day of Badr — the Muslims being three hundred and some, and the idolaters a thousand less a little — the Jews said: This is the one whose banner is not turned back; and they believed. Some of them said: Do not hasten to believe him until there is another battle.
When the Muslims suffered a setback on the day of Uḥud, they called him a liar and turned back. So Allah sent down: Say to the Jews: the idolaters will be defeated and gathered to Hell. In this meaning only the yāʾ is permissible.
Whoever reads with the tāʾ makes the Jews and the idolaters both included in the address. In this meaning sa-yughlabūna and sa-tughlabūna are both permissible, as you say in speech: "Say to ʿAbdullāh that he is standing," and "that you are standing."
In the text of ʿAbdullāh: ﴿قل للذين كفروا إن تنتهوا يغفر لكم ما قد سلف﴾ ("if you desist, what is past will be forgiven you"), and in our reading: "[إن ينتهوا] يُغْفَر لهم ما قد سلف". And in al-Anʿām: ﴿هذا لِلَّه بِزَعْمِهمْ وهَذَا لِشُركَائهم﴾ [Translator's note: so in the text], and in our reading: "لشركائنا".

farraa:13-13.t:
His saying: ﴿قَدْ كَانَ لَكُمْ آيَةٌ فِي فِئَتَيْنِ ٱلْتَقَتَا﴾ — meaning the Prophet, may Allah bless him, his family and his Companions and grant them peace, and the idolaters on the day of Badr.
﴿فِئَةٌ تُقَاتِلُ﴾ was read in the nominative, and it is the proper way of speech, in the sense of: one of them fights in the way of Allah, ﴿وَأُخْرَىٰ كَافِرَةٌ﴾, as a fresh start (istiʾnāf), as the poet said:
فكنتُ كذِى رِجْلينِ رجلٌ صحيحةٌ * ورِجْلٌ رمَى فيها الزّمان فشَلّتِ
(I was like one with two legs: a sound leg, and a leg that time struck so that it withered.)
Had you used the genitive it would be good, referring it back to the first genitive, as though you said: like one with two legs — like one with a sound leg and a sick leg. Likewise the genitive of al-fiʾa and al-ukhrā is permissible on the beginning of the speech.
Had you said: "fiʾatan tuqātilu fī sabīli Allāhi ukhrā kāfiratan" (accusative), it would be correct, on your saying: they met, being different. And the poet said, in the like of that, of what is begun afresh:
إذ مُِتُّ كان الناس نصفين شامتٌ * وآخَرُ مُثْنٍ بالذى كنت أفعل
(When I die, people will be two halves: one gloating, and another praising what I used to do.)
He began the speech after "two halves" and explained it; he meant: some gloating and some not gloating.
The accusative in both is permissible, referring them back to "two halves." And another said:
حتى إذا ما استقلّ النجمُ فى غَلَس * وغودِر البقلُ ملْوِىٌّ ومحصود
(Until, when the Pleiades rose in the last darkness of night, and the herbage was left withered and reaped…)
He explained: some of the herbage is thus, and some of it thus. The accusative is permissible.
Every verb you make act on nouns that have actions [i.e. attributes] which are put in the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) that is not a condition has in it the nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject) and the accusative by connection with what precedes it. Of that: "I saw the people standing and sitting (qāʾiman wa-qāʿidan)," and "qāʾimun wa-qāʿidun," because with the accusative you intended cutting off (qaṭʿ), and the fresh start in cutting off is good.
It is also permissible in what is put in the accusative by the verb; you say: "I think the people are standing and sitting (qiyāman wa-quʿūdan)," and "qiyāmun wa-quʿūdun," and kāna al-qawmu is of the same standing. Likewise: "I saw the people in the house standing and sitting (qiyāman wa-quʿūdan)," "qiyāmun wa-quʿūdun," "qāʾiman wa-qāʿidan," and "qāʾimun wa-qāʿidun"; so you explain it with the singular and the plural. The poet said:
وكتيبةٍ شَعْواء ذات أشِلّة * فيها الفوارس حاسر ومقنَّع
(And many a far-spreading squadron with spear-points, in which are horsemen, bare-headed and helmeted.)
But when you use the accusative as a ḥāl, it is not permissible to explain the plural with two [singulars]; rather you use the plural, saying: "The people are in it standing and sitting (qiyāman wa-quʿūdan)."
As for what is conditional, which cannot be nominative, it is his saying: "Hit your brother when unjust or when doing ill (ẓāliman aw musīʾan)," meaning: hit him in his injustice and in his ill-doing. The nominative is not permissible here in its two ḥāls, because they are tied to the condition. Likewise the plural; you say: "I hit the people stripped or clothed (mujarradīna aw lābisīna)," and "mujarradūna" or "lābisūna" is not permissible, unless you begin afresh and inform, and it is not a condition of the act. Do you not see that if you commanded hitting them in these two states, their [ḥāl] could only be accusative? You say: "Hit the people stripped or clothed (mujarradīna aw lābisīna)," because the condition in the command is binding. In what has passed, you may make it a statement or a condition; therefore both ways are permissible with the past.
His saying: ﴿يَرَوْنَهُمْ مِّثْلَيْهِمْ﴾ — some of those who narrate from Ibn ʿAbbās claimed that he said: the Muslims saw the idolaters, by estimate, as six hundred, while the idolaters were nine hundred and fifty. This is one way. Another view is narrated that seems closer to being correct: that the Muslims saw the idolaters at nine hundred and fifty while the Muslims were few, three hundred and fourteen; therefore He said: ﴿قَدْ كَانَ لَكُمْ﴾ — meaning the Jews — "a sign" in the fewness of the Muslims and the multitude of the idolaters.
If you say: How was it permissible to say "mithlayhim" (twice their number) meaning three times their number? I say: as you say, when you have a slave: "I need the like of him" — you need him and the like of him; and you say: "I need twice my slave (mithlay ʿabdī)," so you need three. A man says: "I have a thousand and I need twice it (mithlayhi)," so he needs three. Since he intended the thousand to be included in the meaning of "the like," the like became two and the two likes three. Similar to it in speech is that you say: "I see you as your like (mithlakum)," as if you said: "I see you as double you (ḍiʿfakum)"; and "I see you as twice your like (mithlaykum)," meaning two doubles of you; this is in the sense of three.
If you say: But He said in Sūrat al-Anfāl: ﴿وإِذْ يُرِيكُموهُمْ إِذِ الْتَقَيْتُمْ فِى أَعْيُنِكُمْ قلِيلاً وَيُقَلّلُكُمْ فى أَعينِهِم﴾ — so how was this a reduction here and a multiplication in the first verse? I say: this is the sign of the Muslims, of which He informed them, and that verse is for the people of disbelief. Besides, you say in speech: "I see your many as few," i.e. it has been made light for me, not that I see three as two.
Whoever reads (tarawnahum) takes it toward the Jews because He addressed them; and whoever says (yarawnahum) is on that [same meaning], as He said: ﴿حتى إِذا كُنْتُمْ فِى الفُلْك وَجَرَيْنَ بِهِم﴾. And if you wish, you make (yarawnahum) refer to the Muslims and not the Jews.
